title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused by check-name-own, naming Lathe's file, and nothing changes
when: Opens a store on the complete product and runs Add check for a product check named `view-unused`, like one of Lathe's checks.
then: Expects it refused with `check-name-own`, naming lathe/data/check.jsonl, one view-unused check left and the product's check.jsonl unchanged.

title: Lathe's checks are read-only
when: Opens a product beside Lathe's checks, tries to change and to remove one of them through Change check and Remove check, and adds a check of the product's own.
then: Expects both refused with `check-read-only`, lathe/data/check.jsonl unchanged, and only the product's check written to its own folder.

title: A check whose summary is not one sentence is refused by check-documented
when: Runs Add check with a summary of two sentences.
then: Expects it refused with `check-documented`, saying the summary has 2 sentences, and no check added.

title: A check whose query is not one SELECT as DuckDB reads it, or names no record and message, or returns a severity its check does not ask for, is refused by check-query-select
when: Runs Add check with a query that is not a SELECT, one of two statements, three that hide a COPY after an escape string, a dollar-quoted string and a comment, four that hold an UPDATE or a DELETE in a WITH, an INSERT in a subquery's WITH and a COPY in a WITH, an INSERT … RETURNING and a MERGE, one without a message column, one returning a severity for a warning check, and an error_or_warning check whose query returns none; then adds checks whose ; sits inside a plain, escape or dollar-quoted string, a comment, or ends the query.
then: Expects each of the first refused with `check-query-select` and its own message, and the product's check.jsonl unchanged; expects each of the last added as written.

title: A product has at most one settings row
when: Runs the Product setting rule over two settings rows of one product and one of another, then loads the two rows of one product from the file.
then: Expects one `product-setting-one` problem, on the second row of the first product; loaded from the file, the second row is refused by the primary key, naming line 1.

title: A check's query reads no file, URL, extension or setting outside the database, and Lathe's checks and coverage run as before
when: Loads the complete product with checks of its own that read the process's environment, a file, a folder listing, a URL, a file planted in DuckDB's temporary folder and the settings, with HTTP_PROXY set to a URL with a password; runs COPY, EXPORT, read_text, read_csv, read_blob and COPY of the schema cache's file, ATTACH of a file, INSTALL, LOAD, and SET, SET GLOBAL, RESET and PRAGMA of each sealing setting on a connection to the loaded data; seals a database whose settings are locked already; loads checks that UPDATE coverage_item and DELETE from coverage_gap inside a WITH, beside a technical file left out, and runs a DELETE inside a WITH as a check on the loaded data; and loads a check row that hides a COPY to a file after an escape string.
then: Expects each reading check to report that it could not run, with DuckDB's Permission Error; the settings read as sealed, with no temporary folder, no allowed directory or path, no proxy and no password; Lathe's own problems, coverage and chains the same as without the product's checks; each statement refused, no file written and the data still read; the locked database refused with `check-query-sealed`; the changing checks refused at load by `check-query-select` with no coverage claimed, and at their run before they bind, the data unchanged and no transaction left open; and the hiding row refused by `check-query-select`, the file unchanged.

title: There is always a tab: closing activates the right neighbor, else the left, and closing the last leaves one tab on the product
when: Closes the active first tab of three, then the rightmost, then the last.
then: Expects the right neighbor active after the first close, the left neighbor after the second, and after the last one tab on the product. Unknown keys change nothing.

title: Each tab's place is its own, duplicating copies it with its history, and a stored set is read back with anything malformed dropped
when: Changes one tab's place, duplicates it, and reads back a stored set.
then: Expects the other tab's place unchanged; the duplicate after it with the same place and history, then going its own way; and a stored set read back with a bad path, a bad place and a bad history dropped, and an unknown active tab replaced by the first.

title: The Space commands keep the spaces through SpaceRepository, and a last page that is not a page of a space is refused
when: Remembers a page in a space, notes the spaces listed, then remembers `/` as a space's last page.
then: Expects each kept under its key, and `/` refused with its reason and nothing saved.

title: The Nav row commands keep the rows through NavRowRepository, and a row without a key or neither open nor folded is refused
when: Folds and unfolds rows and sections, opens a branch, then holds rows with an empty key and a section neither open nor folded.
then: Expects each kept, and each broken row refused with its reason.

title: The Session settings commands each keep one setting, and a width outside its limits or a layout or baseline the app does not have is refused
when: Runs each Session settings command, then holds a card 10 px wide, a chat 2000 px wide, a radial layout and an unknown baseline.
then: Expects each setting kept in session storage, and each broken one refused with its reason.

title: A second handler of an endpoint is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second handler of an endpoint.
then: Expects each refused with `one-endpoint-handler` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second adapter of an integration is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second adapter of an integration.
then: Expects each refused with `one-adapter` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second value type of a value object, or a second test of a constraint, is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second value type of a value object, then a second test of a constraint.
then: Expects each refused with `value-object-one-each` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second data model of an entity, or a second rule or test of an invariant, is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second data model of an entity, then a second rule and a second test of an invariant.
then: Expects each refused with `aggregate-one-each` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second predicate or test of a specification is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second predicate, then a second test, of a specification.
then: Expects each refused with `specification-one-each` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second handler of a command, a second test of a policy, and a policy hearing two events are refused
when: Runs Add a command handler for a command that has one and Add a policy test for a policy that has one; then loads a policy that hears a second event of its domain.
then: Expects both commands refused with `command-one-each` and its message, and the loaded link refused with `unique` in `hears.jsonl`.

title: A second projection or reader of a read model, or a second handler of a query, is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second projection of a read model, a second reader of it, then a second handler of a query.
then: Expects each refused with `read-model-one-each` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second event type of a domain event is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second event type of a domain event.
then: Expects each refused with `one-event-type` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second service of a domain service is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second service of a domain service.
then: Expects each refused with `one-service` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: An aggregate with two roots is refused, one with none is not
when: Adds a second root entity to an aggregate and changes a child to a root, then loads data files that give an aggregate two roots; adds a child to an aggregate with no root.
then: Expects each refused as aggregate-root with its reason and no file changed, the load refused naming aggregate.jsonl and its line, and the aggregate with no root kept.

title: An entity field with two types, or none, is refused by entity-field-one-type
when: Runs Change entity giving the loan entity a field with a basic type and an aggregate, then one with no type.
then: Expects each refused with `entity-field-one-type`, naming the field and what types it, and entity_field unchanged.

title: An entity field named like another of its entity but for spacing or case is refused by entity-field-name
when: Runs Change entity with fields Loan ID and ` loan id `, then with Loan ID and Loan IDs.
then: Expects the first refused with `entity-field-name` and entity_field unchanged, and the second saved.

title: A second capability at a position of its domain is refused by capability-position; another position is not
when: With a domain that has a capability at position 1, runs Add capability at position 1, then at 2.
then: Expects the first refused with `capability-position`, naming the capability already there, and the second added.

title: A value object field with two types, none, or its own value object is refused by value-object-field-one-type
when: Runs Change value object with a field typed by text and an aggregate, one with no type, and one typed by its own value object.
then: Expects each refused with `value-object-field-one-type` and its own message, and value_object_field unchanged.

title: A value object field named like another of its value object but for case is refused by value-object-field-name
when: Runs Change value object with fields Address and ADDRESS.
then: Expects it refused with `value-object-field-name` and value_object_field unchanged.

title: A domain event field with two types, or none, is refused by event-field-one-type
when: Runs Change domain event with a field typed by text and an aggregate, then one with no type.
then: Expects each refused with `event-field-one-type` and event_field unchanged.

title: A domain event field named like another of its event but for case is refused by event-field-name
when: Runs Change domain event with fields Loan ID and LOAN ID.
then: Expects it refused with `event-field-name` and event_field unchanged.

title: A read model field with two types, or none, is refused by read-model-field-one-type
when: Runs Change read model with a field typed by a whole number and a value object, then one with no type.
then: Expects each refused with `read-model-field-one-type` and read_model_field unchanged.

title: A read model field named like another of its read model but for case is refused by read-model-field-name
when: Runs Change read model with fields Days overdue and days overdue.
then: Expects it refused with `read-model-field-name` and read_model_field unchanged.

title: has_one or has_many to an entity of another aggregate is refused by has-crosses-aggregate
when: Loads the complete product with a has_many from the loan entity to an entity of another aggregate.
then: Expects the load refused with `has-crosses-aggregate`, naming both aggregates and saying to type a field by the other aggregate instead.

title: A second persists link of a repository is refused by repository-persists-one
when: Runs the rule over two persists links of one repository and one of another.
then: Expects one `repository-persists-one` problem, on the second link of the first repository.

title: A second repository for one aggregate is refused, and so are a second aggregate for one repository and a second repository of one identifier
when: Loads a second repository persisting an aggregate that already has one, a repository persisting a second aggregate, and a second repository with the same title and file as the first.
then: Expects `unique` refusals on `persists.jsonl` for the shared target and the shared source, and `title-unique` on both repositories of one identifier.

title: A term whose links lead back to it is refused, naming the loop, and no file changes
when: Change term links Entity to Aggregate while Aggregate builds on Entity, Add term adds a term building on itself through a term of another domain, and data holding a loop is loaded.
then: Each is refused with term-builds-on-itself naming the loop (Aggregate → Entity → Aggregate), the builds_on file is unchanged, and the load names the loop once.

title: A policy hearing another domain's unpublished event is refused
when: Changes a policy to hear, and adds one hearing, an unpublished event of another domain; then loads data files where a policy hears it, and again once the event is published.
then: Expects each refused as policy-hears-published with its reason and no file changed, the load refused naming hears.jsonl and its line, and the published event to load.

title: A read model fed by another domain's unpublished event is refused
when: Changes a read model to be fed by, and adds one fed by, an unpublished event of another domain; then loads data files where a read model is fed by it, and again once the event is published.
then: Expects each refused as read-model-fed-by-published with its reason and no file changed, the load refused naming fed_by.jsonl and its line, and the published event to load.

title: A theme exports as a versioned file and imports back, and anything but known tokens is refused
when: Reads a partial theme file that sets only the light `--ink`.
then: Expects the missing `--paper` taken from Lathe: `#F4F6F5` in light and `#11171B` in dark.

title: A built-in theme is changed only through a copy, and reset puts the copy back to its built-in
when: Duplicates Workshop in Appearance, changes the copy's light accent, then resets it to Workshop.
then: Expects the copy in use as `custom-workshop-copy`, its stylesheet to carry `--steel: #123456;` after the change and `--steel: #9C3F17;` after Reset to Workshop, the editor still titled `Edit “Workshop copy”`, and Workshop's own light accent still `#9C3F17`.

title: Deleting the theme in use puts Lathe back in use
when: Duplicates Workshop in Appearance, which puts the copy in use, then deletes the copy after confirming.
then: Expects the address back at `?panel=appearance` and the theme in use `lathe`.

title: A second launch or a folder from Finder goes to the running app, which opens or focuses its window
when: Records `/work/shop` as open in a window, then looks up the window for `/work/shop/`, `/work/./shop` and `/work/other`.
then: Expects the window open for `/work/shop` found for `/work/shop/` and `/work/./shop`, and none for another folder.

title: In development the window uses the 5199 server only when it answers for the opened folder
when: Asks for a free port, then for one avoiding 5199 and a port another server holds.
then: Expects the shared port to be 5199, and neither free port to be 5199 or the held port.

title: The recent folders list puts the latest first, each folder once, at most 10
when: Adds folders to the list, adds one again, adds twelve, and reads saved lists with junk in them.
then: Expects a new folder first; a folder added again moved to the top (with a trailing slash too) rather than listed twice; at most 10 kept, the oldest dropped; and a saved list read with non-strings, empty strings and repeats dropped, its order kept and cut to 10.

title: A panel's width stays within its limits: a resize is brought within them and a width outside them is refused
when: Resizes the nav past its limits, shows and hides it, then holds a width of 10 px.
then: Expects the width kept at its limit, the collapsed state kept, and 10 px refused with its reason.

title: A custom editor has its command
when: Chooses Cursor, then a custom editor with no command, then opens a missing settings file.
then: Expects Cursor kept with the rest of the file, the custom editor refused with its reason, and the missing file written with an empty command to fill in.

title: The editor is one Lathe knows
when: Holds settings naming an unknown editor, and chooses one.
then: Expects both refused with the reason, and nothing saved.

title: No two shortcuts share a key where both apply: binding one that another has is refused naming it, and Swap hands the key over
when: Binds Ctrl+Shift+M (Open Checks) and then G (the start of g then c) to Show or hide the navigation, binds a key where no other shortcut applies, then swaps Ctrl+Shift+M in place of Ctrl+B and resets the navigation.
then: Expects both refused naming both shortcuts with nothing saved, the free key kept, after the swap the navigation on Ctrl+Shift+M and Open Checks on Ctrl+B, and the reset refused as Ctrl+B is taken.

title: A key the browser or the system keeps cannot be bound
when: Binds Ctrl+W off a Mac and Cmd+Q on a Mac to Show or hide the navigation, then Ctrl+L on a Mac to Go home.
then: Expects Ctrl+W and ⌘Q refused with their reason, and Ctrl+L kept on a Mac, where Ctrl is the Control key.

title: Every shortcut keeps a key unless it is unbound on purpose
when: Removes Quick open's Ctrl+K, then its Ctrl+P, then Ctrl+P again saying to leave it without a key.
then: Expects Ctrl+K removed, the last key refused with its reason, then Quick open kept without a key (stored as null).

title: Only the app's own shortcuts can be bound: not the browser's, nor an ARIA control's
when: Binds a key to Go back (browser), to the tree's Expand the row and to a shortcut that does not exist, then stores such bindings by hand.
then: Expects each refused with its reason, and the hand-stored ones dropped as the bindings load.

title: Voice phrases have one to three words, and no two say the same
when: Checks the default phrases, then a blank wake phrase, two commands with the same words, a four-word command, and a command that is the wake phrase.
then: Expects the defaults accepted and each other one refused with its reason, under the rule voice-phrases-distinct.

title: Opening a session ends the one the chat ran, and a chat kept under another folder or running another window's session is refused
when: Opens a session in a folder's chat, opens another in it, and holds chats kept under the wrong folder or sharing a session to the rule.
then: The first session is closed before the second opens, and the rule refuses each wrong chat with its reason.

title: A record of a kind its file titles takes its title from the file, and a differing title is refused
when: Declares a module kind whose required file field titles it, adds a module with no title, changes its file, then adds and changes one with a title that differs; then loads declarations with an optional titling field and with two.
then: Expects the title to equal the file after each write, each differing title refused with title-from-field and no file changed, and both declarations refused with product-kind.

title: A step with an ID that is not its journey's and S<nn> is refused
when: Adds a step to TL-JR01 with the ID TL-JR01-X1, and one with the ID TL-JR02-S01.
then: Expects each refused with a journey-step-id reason naming the ID the step must have.

title: A journey test with an ID that is not its journey's and T is refused
when: Adds a journey test to a journey with the ID TL-JR01-T2.
then: Expects it refused with a journey-test-id reason naming TL-JR01-T.

title: Two steps at one position of a path are refused, the path compared trimmed and in any letter case
when: Adds a step to TL-JR01 at position 1 of the path ' Main ', where TL-JR01-S01 is on main at position 1, then at position 1 of another path.
then: Expects the first refused with a journey-step-position reason naming TL-JR01-S01, and the second added.

title: A second journey test of a journey is refused
when: Adds a second journey test to a journey that has one.
then: Expects it refused with a journey-one-each reason naming the journey and its test.

title: A journey serving another product's outcome, or carrying out another product's use case, is refused
when: Adds a journey serving an outcome of another product, and links a step to a use case of another product.
then: Expects each refused with a journey-in-product reason naming both products.

title: A step carrying out a record that does not exist is refused, and so is removing one a step carries out
when: Links a step to an ID no use case or policy has, then removes the policy a step carries out.
then: Expects the link refused, and the removal refused naming the step.

title: An interface listing a role its product lacks is refused, and so is dropping a role an interface lists
when: Adds an interface listing a role its product lacks, changes an interface's roles to one, then changes the product's roles to drop one an interface lists.
then: Expects an interface-actor-role refusal naming the role and the product's roles each time, and the interface's roles unchanged.

title: A product kind named like a Lathe table, or under no kind, is refused by product-kind-declared
when: Runs Declare product kind named aggregate, then record_id, then under gadget.
then: Expects each refused with `product-kind-declared` and its own message, and product_kind unchanged.

title: A new relation's pairs with different labels, a pair naming no kind, or a pair Lathe's relation's ends do not accept is refused by product-relation-own
when: Runs Declare product relation with a second pair of documents under other labels, one to a kind that does not exist, and a pair of Lathe's reads from a CLI command to an endpoint.
then: Expects each refused with `product-relation-own` and its own message, and product_relation unchanged.

title: A product kind, kind field or relation without a description is refused by product-declaration-described
when: Holds the product to its rules with its kind, kind field and relation each described by a blank.
then: Expects three `product-declaration-described` problems, one naming each declaration.

title: An open question owned by a role its product lacks is refused
when: Adds a question owned by a role its product lacks, then changes the product's roles to drop one a question names.
then: Expects a question-owner-role refusal naming the question, the owner and the product's roles, and no file changed.

title: A record of a product's kind under another product's domain is refused
when: Adds a record of TL's kind under another product's domain with Add an extension record.
then: Expects a product-kind-product refusal with its reason, and no file changed.

title: A second table of an entity or a read model is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second table of an entity, then of a read model.
then: Expects each refused with `one-table-each` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A table for an entity stored in its root's table is refused, and so is an entity's table that is a view
when: Adds a table for a child entity stored in its root's table and changes an entity's table to a view; then loads data files with such a table, a root marked as stored in its root's table, and an entity's table stored as a view or a materialized view.
then: Expects the add refused as entity-table with its reason and the change as a check refusal, no file changed, and each load refused: entity-table naming table.jsonl, a check refusal for the root, the view and the materialized view.

title: A table's second primary key is refused, and so is a key whose parts do not fit its type
when: Changes a table to have two primary keys; then loads data files with a second primary key, and keys whose parts do not fit their type: an index with a condition, a primary key naming an invariant, a foreign key with no target table and an index with one.
then: Expects the change refused as one-primary-key with its reason and no file changed, the load refused as one-primary-key on the table, and a check refusal for each misplaced part.

title: A foreign key to another domain's table is refused
when: Changes a table to have a foreign key to another domain's table, then loads data files with one.
then: Expects the change refused as foreign-key-crosses-domain with its reason and no file changed, and the load refused naming table_key.jsonl.

title: A key of or to a table kept outside a database is refused
when: Changes a table with keys to each storage outside a database, and gives a table a foreign key to one; then loads data files where a table with keys, and one a foreign key points at, is kept outside a database, and again without those keys.
then: Expects each refused as key-outside-database with its reason and no file changed, the load refused once per key, and the data to load once the keys are gone.

title: A setting value gives a value, never none and never an empty one
when: Loads setting values with no value and with an empty value.
then: Expects each refused, and a value to load.

title: A second value of one setting from one follower is refused by setting-value-own-pattern
when: Runs Change setting values giving the follower's setting record two values.
then: Expects it refused with `setting-value-own-pattern` and the setting value unchanged.

title: A setting value for a setting its pattern lacks, or for a pattern its follower does not follow, is refused by setting-value-of-followed-setting
when: Runs Change setting values and Follow pattern with a setting the pattern lacks, then loads the every-kind fixture with its follows links removed.
then: Expects both commands refused with `setting-value-of-followed-setting` and nothing changed, and the load refused by the foreign key on setting_value line 1.

title: a step fulfilling another use case's requirement
when: Loads a step of one use case's flow that fulfills a requirement of another use case.
then: Expects a `step-fulfills-own-use-case` refusal on the `fulfills` line, naming the requirement and its use case.

title: A second flow of a use case, a second test of a flow, and a second invoke of a step, are refused
when: Runs Add a flow for a use case that has one, Add a flow test for a flow that has one, and gives a step a second invoke.
then: Expects both commands refused with `use-case-one-each` and its message, and each loaded row refused by its unique key underneath.

title: A second test of a pattern rule for one domain is refused
when: On a store holding one record of every kind, so each parent already has its one, runs the command that adds a second test of a pattern rule for a domain that already has one.
then: Expects each refused with `pattern-rule-test-per-domain` and a message naming the parent and the record it already has, before the unique key underneath is reached.

title: A second step at a position of a path, compared trimmed and in any letter case, is refused by step-position; another path may use it
when: With a step at position 1 of path main, runs Add flow step at position 1 of path ` Main`, then of path refused.
then: Expects the first refused with `step-position`, naming the step already there, and the second added.

title: A use case actor its product lacks is refused, and so is dropping a role an actor names
when: Changes a use case's actors to add a role its product lacks, adds a use case with such an actor, then changes the product's roles to drop one a use case names.
then: Expects a use-case-actor-role refusal naming the role and the product's roles each time, and the use case's actors unchanged.

title: A flow whose ID is not its use case's and FL is refused
when: Adds a flow FL02 to a use case with Add a flow.
then: Expects a flow-id-interface refusal saying its ID is the use case's FL01.
